analysis:
On 16 July 2009 Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and his Pakistani counterpart Yusuf Raza Gilani issued a joint statement at Sharm el-Sheikh. The text recorded that Prime Minister Gilani "mentioned that Pakistan has some information on threats in Balochistan and other areas", and stated that action on terrorism should not be linked to the composite dialogue.

In Parliament on 29 July 2009 Manmohan Singh defended the statement, saying "there has been no dilution of our position in this regard", that India had no interest in destabilising Pakistan, and that dialogue remained the way forward.

Opposition parties and several commentators said the text reversed India's earlier public position linking progress in dialogue to Pakistan's action on terrorism and gave Pakistan a handle on Balochistan. The government maintained the reference did not amount to an admission. The joint statement text and the Prime Minister's Parliament statement are both matters of record; the characterisation of "no dilution" remains contested.
